docs.text: Approximate nearest neighbor search trades a small amount of recall for large speedups over exact brute-force scans.
HNSW builds a multi-layer navigable small-world graph so queries descend from sparse top layers to dense bottom layers.
Product quantization compresses high-dimensional vectors into compact codes, shrinking the memory footprint of an index.
Cosine similarity measures the angle between two embedding vectors and ignores their magnitude.
IVF indexes partition the vector space into Voronoi cells and probe only the nearest cells at query time.
Recall at k for an ANN index is the fraction of true nearest neighbors that appear in the returned top-k list.
sqlite-vec stores embeddings inside a virtual table so a single SQLite file holds both rows and their vectors.
Embedding models map text into a dense vector where semantically similar passages land close together.
A flat brute-force index computes the distance to every stored vector and is exact but slow at scale.
Reranking a candidate list with a cross-encoder improves precision at the top after a fast first-stage retrieval.
An ACID transaction guarantees atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability even when the system crashes.
A B-tree index keeps keys sorted on disk so range scans and point lookups stay logarithmic.
Write-ahead logging records changes to a durable log before applying them to the main data files.
Normalization splits data into related tables to remove redundancy and avoid update anomalies.
An OLAP column store keeps each column contiguous, which speeds up aggregate scans over few columns.
Multiversion concurrency control lets readers see a consistent snapshot without blocking writers.
A foreign key constraint enforces that a referencing row points at an existing row in another table.
Sharding splits a large table across multiple machines by a partition key to scale writes horizontally.
A materialized view caches the result of an expensive query and is refreshed on a schedule.
SQLite stores an entire relational database, including its schema and indexes, in one cross-platform file.
The Maillard reaction browns seared meat and bread crust by reacting amino acids with sugars under heat.
Letting a roast rest after cooking lets the juices redistribute so they do not run out when you slice it.
Emulsifying oil into egg yolk slowly produces a stable mayonnaise that does not separate.
Blanching vegetables briefly in boiling water then shocking them in ice keeps their color bright.
Kneading bread dough develops gluten strands that trap gas and give the loaf its chewy structure.
Searing at high heat creates a flavorful crust, while a gentle braise breaks down tough connective tissue.
Salting meat ahead of time draws moisture out and then back in, seasoning it deeply and improving texture.
A roux of flour cooked in fat thickens sauces and gives gumbo its nutty depth.
Proofing yeast dough in a warm place lets carbon dioxide expand the gluten network before baking.
Deglazing a hot pan with wine lifts the browned fond into a rich pan sauce.
Compound interest grows a balance faster than simple interest because earnings themselves earn returns.
Diversifying a portfolio across uncorrelated assets reduces overall volatility without cutting expected return much.
A bond's price moves inversely to prevailing interest rates because its fixed coupon becomes relatively less attractive.
An index fund passively tracks a market benchmark and charges far lower fees than active management.
Inflation erodes the purchasing power of cash, so money held idle loses real value over time.
Dollar-cost averaging invests a fixed amount on a schedule, smoothing out the effect of price swings.
The price-to-earnings ratio compares a stock's price to its annual earnings per share.
A central bank raising its policy rate tends to cool borrowing, spending, and ultimately inflation.
Liquidity is how quickly an asset can be sold for cash without moving its price.
Leverage amplifies both gains and losses because borrowed money magnifies the position's exposure.
Gradient descent iteratively nudges model weights in the direction that most reduces the loss.
Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training noise and fails to generalize to new data.
Regularization such as weight decay penalizes large parameters to curb overfitting.
A transformer uses self-attention to weigh how much each token should attend to every other token.
Backpropagation applies the chain rule to compute gradients of the loss with respect to each weight.
Dropout randomly zeroes activations during training so the network does not rely on any single unit.
A confusion matrix breaks predictions into true and false positives and negatives for each class.
Transfer learning fine-tunes a model pretrained on a large corpus for a smaller downstream task.
Batch normalization rescales layer inputs to stabilize and speed up training.
Cross-validation rotates which fold of data is held out so the score is less sensitive to one split.
The CAP theorem says a partitioned distributed store must choose between consistency and availability.
The Raft protocol elects a leader that replicates a log to followers to keep replicas consistent.
Eventual consistency lets replicas diverge briefly but guarantees they converge if writes stop.
A vector clock tracks causal ordering of events across nodes without a shared global clock.
Idempotent operations can be retried safely because repeating them produces the same result.
Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes onto a ring so adding a node moves only a small fraction of keys.
A two-phase commit coordinator asks all participants to prepare, then tells them all to commit or abort.
Quorum reads and writes overlap enough replicas to guarantee a read sees the latest acknowledged write.
Backpressure slows a fast producer when a downstream consumer cannot keep up, preventing overload.
A heartbeat message lets a cluster detect that a node has failed when the beats stop arriving.
TCP provides a reliable ordered byte stream by acknowledging segments and retransmitting lost ones.
DNS resolves a human-readable domain name into the IP address a client needs to connect.
TLS encrypts a connection and authenticates the server using a certificate signed by a trusted authority.
The three-way handshake of SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK establishes a TCP connection before data flows.
A router forwards packets between networks by consulting its routing table for the best next hop.
UDP sends datagrams without connection setup or delivery guarantees, trading reliability for low latency.
HTTP is a stateless request-response protocol layered on top of a reliable transport like TCP.
Network address translation lets many private hosts share one public IP address.
A content delivery network caches copies of assets near users to cut latency.
The maximum transmission unit is the largest packet a link can carry without fragmentation.
Hashing a password with a slow salted function like bcrypt resists offline brute-force cracking.
Public-key cryptography uses a key pair so anyone can encrypt to you but only your private key decrypts.
A SQL injection attack smuggles malicious input into a query that the database then executes.
Multi-factor authentication combines something you know with something you have to verify identity.
The principle of least privilege grants each component only the permissions it actually needs.
A digital signature proves a message came from the holder of a private key and was not altered.
Cross-site scripting injects attacker-controlled script into a page so it runs in another user's browser.
A replay attack captures a valid message and resends it later to impersonate the original sender.
Rate limiting caps how many requests a client may make, blunting brute-force and denial-of-service attempts.
End-to-end encryption keeps a message readable only by the sender and intended recipient, not the relay.
Photosynthesis converts sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into glucose and releases oxygen.
DNA stores genetic information as a sequence of four bases paired across a double helix.
Mitochondria generate most of a cell's ATP through aerobic respiration and are called its powerhouse.
Natural selection favors heritable traits that improve survival and reproduction in an environment.
Enzymes are protein catalysts that lower the activation energy of biochemical reactions.
Messenger RNA carries the instructions transcribed from DNA to the ribosome where proteins are built.
Osmosis moves water across a semipermeable membrane toward the side with more dissolved solute.
A virus hijacks a host cell's machinery to replicate because it cannot reproduce on its own.
Cellular respiration breaks down glucose with oxygen to release energy stored as ATP.
The immune system's antibodies bind specific antigens to mark pathogens for destruction.
The printing press let Gutenberg mass-produce books, accelerating the spread of ideas across Europe.
The Industrial Revolution shifted production from handcraft to steam-powered factories in the eighteenth century.
The Roman Republic gave way to imperial rule after Augustus consolidated power.
The Silk Road carried goods and ideas between China and the Mediterranean for centuries.
The fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 marked the symbolic end of the Cold War division of Europe.
The French Revolution overthrew the monarchy and proclaimed liberty, equality, and fraternity.
The Renaissance revived classical art and learning, beginning in the Italian city-states.
The Magna Carta limited the English king's power and seeded ideas of constitutional government.
The transatlantic telegraph cable first let messages cross the ocean in minutes instead of weeks.
The Black Death killed a large share of medieval Europe's population in the fourteenth century.
An octave doubles a note's frequency, and the two pitches sound like the same note higher or lower.
A major chord stacks a root, a major third, and a perfect fifth into a bright-sounding triad.
Tempo is the speed of the beat, measured in beats per minute.
Counterpoint weaves two or more independent melodic lines that sound good together.
Equal temperament tunes the octave into twelve equally spaced semitones so any key sounds in tune.
A time signature tells how many beats fill each measure and which note value counts as one beat.
Reverb simulates the reflections of sound in a space, adding depth to a recording.
A minor key tends to sound darker or sadder than its parallel major key.
Syncopation places accents on the off-beats, giving rhythm a surprising push.
Harmonics are the higher frequencies above a fundamental pitch that give an instrument its timbre.
Greenhouse gases trap outgoing infrared radiation, warming the planet's surface.
Carbon dioxide released by burning fossil fuels is the largest human driver of global warming.
Melting land ice raises sea levels, threatening low-lying coastal communities.
The ocean absorbs much of the excess heat and carbon dioxide, which also makes seawater more acidic.
Solar and wind power generate electricity without emitting the carbon dioxide that fossil fuels do.
A carbon sink such as a forest stores more carbon than it releases.
The albedo effect means bright ice reflects sunlight, so melting ice exposes darker water that absorbs more heat.
Methane is a far more potent greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide over a short timescale.
Climate feedback loops can amplify warming, as thawing permafrost releases yet more greenhouse gas.
Adaptation measures like sea walls and drought-resistant crops cope with climate impacts already underway.
